provisions.summary: Repeals the scheduled standard deduction increases for tax years after 2027, 2029 and 2030, leaving the 2026 amounts ($16,000 joint, $12,000 head of household, $8,000 single) in force for 2027-2031.
provisions.quote: For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025: (i) $16,000 in the case of a joint return

provisions.summary: Repeals the scheduled bracket schedules for tax years after 2026 and 2028, leaving the schedule for years after December 31, 2024 in force through 2031.
provisions.quote: In the case of any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024: If the taxable income is: The tax shall be: Not over $19,200 1.40% of taxable income

provisions.summary: Raises the child and dependent care credit's applicable percentage to 50% reduced 1 point per $3,000 of AGI over $150,000, with a 15% floor. The spec cannot model this credit.
provisions.quote: equal to fifty per cent reduced by one percentage point for each $3,000, or fraction thereof, by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000

provisions.summary: Disallows the child and dependent care credit for ten taxable years after a final decision that a claim was fraudulent, and for two years after a final decision disallowing a claim. The spec cannot model this.
provisions.quote: The period of ten taxable years after the most recent taxable year for which there was a final administrative or judicial decision that the taxpayer's claim for credit under this section was due to fraud

provisions.summary: Moves the Act 163 sunset from December 31, 2027 to December 31, 2032, which keeps the EITC at 40% of federal and the larger food/excise credit table through tax year 2031.
provisions.quote: on December 31, [2027,] 2032, this Act shall be repealed and sections 235-55.6(c), 235-55.75(a), and 235-55.85(b)

notes: Section 3 defines 'adjusted gross income' by reference to the Internal Revenue Code, which is a definition rather than a provision. Section 6 applies section 3 to tax years after 2026 and repeals it on December 31, 2032, so the child and dependent care changes also sunset after 2031 and fall outside the spec. Sections 1 and 2 have no sunset. The standard deduction vintages are flat over 2027-2031 because the repealed steps are the only ones that would have changed them. The bracket schedule left in force is the one for years after December 31, 2024. The bill's 2026-and-later schedules are bracketed (repealed), and no schedule heading beyond 2024 remains. The sunset extension is effective from the bill's approval, but its modeled effect only appears from tax year 2028, since Act 163's expansions already apply through 2027.
